No, that is not true. According to Swiss law (the Swiss Citizenship Act), the minimum residency requirements for naturalization are generally 10 years for foreign nationals from non-EU/EFTA countries (holding a B permit), plus an additional 3 years of continuous residency in the same Swiss canton and municipality immediately before the application. This totals **13 years** of residence, not 12.

Additionally, naturalization requires fulfilling several other conditions, including integration (language skills, participation in Swiss society, knowledge of Swiss customs and institutions), financial independence, and a clean criminal record.

Please note that requirements may vary slightly between cantons and municipalities, so it is always advisable to consult the local authorities for precise details.
